Package ca.refundr.highspring.api.resource.version1

Class Version1Resource

java.lang.Object
ca.refundr.highspring.api.resource.AbstractResource
ca.refundr.highspring.api.resource.AbstractChildResource<RootResource>
ca.refundr.highspring.api.resource.version1.Version1Resource
public final class Version1Resource extends AbstractChildResource<RootResource>
Version 1 of the public API — everything under /v1/.

Role in the HTTP chain

RootResource owns /. This class owns the next segment v1/. When the filter asks for v1/products/:

  1. Root matches and strips nothing special (root path is "").
  2. Root’s child list finds this Version1Resource because the path starts with v1/.
  3. This class strips v1/ and looks at the remainder products/.
  4. getDescendantByPath(String) tries each registered child until one matches.

Map of /v1 children

   /v1/auth/...        AuthResource       Google login + logout
   /v1/me/             MeResource         current session user
   /v1/products/       ProductsResource   catalog (read-only)
   /v1/cart/...        CartResource       persisted cart + checkout
   /v1/purchases/...   PurchasesResource  create/fetch purchases
   /v1/admin/...       AdminResource      ADMIN-only tools

How to add a new endpoint

  1. Create a class extending AbstractChildResource<Version1Resource> (or nest under an existing child like AuthResource).
  2. Implement getRelativePath() — must end with / (e.g. "wishlist/").
  3. Register it in getDescendantByPath(String) below.
  4. Override httpGet/httpPost/… and add those methods to supportedMethods in the constructor.

There is no central “routes file”. This method is the route table for v1.

      protected <T extends AbstractResource> T getDescendantByPath(String relativePath)
      Route table for everything under /v1/.

      Order rarely matters unless two children claim the same prefix (avoid that). Each supplier builds a candidate; getDescendantFromChildren returns the first match.
